'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|ISIL-K]] militants open fire against a [[Taliban]] vehicle at a gas station in [[Jalalabad]], killing two Taliban members, a gas station attendant, and a child. Two bombs also explode nearby to two more Taliban vehicles, killing another child and injuring three more Taliban members. [https://www.firstpost.com/world/two-taliban-fighters-among-five-killed-in-fresh-attacks-in-jalalabad-9987431.html (First Post)]
**ISIS-K militants kill four [[Christians|Christian]] Afghan men after stopping their vehicle and then shooting the victims. [https://www.mnnonline.org/news/isis-kills-four-afghan-christians/ (Mission Network News)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi forces]] capture the [[Bayhan District]] in [[Yemen]]'s [[Shabwah Governorate]] where oil fields are located and continue their advance into neighboring [[Usaylan District]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-ph/news/national/rebels-seize-yemen-oil-fields/ar-AAOI7P5?ocid=BingNewsSearch (Xinhua via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[German police|Authorities in Germany]] link a belief in [[COVID-19 conspiracy theories]] and [[far-right extremism]] as motives behind the killing of a cashier in [[Idar-Oberstein]], [[Rhineland-Palatinate]], four days ago. The 20-year-old student employee was murdered at the shop where he worked by a man who [[Mask refusal|refused to wear a mask]]. [[Far-right extremists]] praise the killing and make denigratory comments about the victim. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-58635103 (BBC News)]
*Gunmen open fire against a vehicle carrying Serhiy Shefir, an official close to [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President]] [[Volodymyr Zelensky]], near the village of Lisnyky, outside of [[Kyiv]], wounding the driver of the car. The attack is deemed an [[list of people who survived assassination attempts|assassination attempt]] against Shefir. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/22/shots-fired-at-car-carrying-ukrainian-presidents-aide (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Mansfield earthquake]]
**A magnitude 5.8 [[list of earthquakes in Australia|earthquake]] strikes the [[Alpine National Park]] in [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], [[Australia]], with tremors felt throughout the state and in parts of [[New South Wales]], the [[Australian Capital Territory]], [[South Australia]] and [[Tasmania]]. Some buildings in [[Melbourne]] are damaged but no casualties are reported. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-09-22/earthquake-victoria-melbourne-nsw-sydney-canberra-act/100481732 (ABC News Australia)]
*A magnitude 6.5 [[list of earthquakes in Nicaragua|earthquake]] strikes off the coast of [[Nicaragua]], measuring {{convert|40|km}} in depth. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/magnitude-65-earthquake-strikes-near-coast-nicaragua-emsc-2021-09-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[UNICEF]] reports that most infants in at least 91 countries suffer from [[malnourishment]] and [[food insecurity]]. The [[United Nations]] [[Food and Agriculture Organization]] estimated last week that about 811 million people globally are affected by hunger. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2021/sep/22/most-infants-in-91-countries-are-malnourished-warns-unicef (''The Guardian'')]
*A Russian [[An-26]] transport aircraft, believed to have six people on board, disappears while flying at an [[Low altitude|ultralow altitude]] of 600 meters. The plane went off radar some {{convert|38|km}} from [[Khabarovsk Novy Airport|Khabarovsk airport]] in southeastern [[Russia]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/russian-plane-disappears-with-six-on-board/a-59264668 (DW)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia (country)|COVID-19 pandemic in Georgia]]
****[[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] surpasses 600,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://apa.az/en/xeber/europe/georgias-coronavirus-cases-exceed-600-thousand-358330 (Azeri Press Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports its lowest number of active COVID-19 case in 186 days with the daily positivity rate recorded at 1.69%. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus-pandemic/india-reports-its-lowest-active-covid-cases-in-186-days (''Khaleej Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports a record 1,457 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, surpassing the previous record of 1,426 cases set in April 2020, and thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 81,356. [https://news.yahoo.com/1457-new-covid-cases-3-more-deaths-reported-in-singapore-150309485.html (Yahoo! News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
****[[Michigan]] surpasses one million confirmed cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.clickondetroit.com/health/2021/09/22/michigan-surpasses-1-million-covid-cases-reports-6079-new-cases-81-deaths-over-past-2-days/#// (WDIV-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[Food and Drug Administration]] officially authorizes the usage of a third dosage of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]] as a [[Booster_dose#COVID-19_booster_dose|booster shot]] for individuals still considered vulnerable to COVID-19. Among those eligible are health care workers and senior citizens who have been fully inoculated with the vaccine for at least six months. [https://www.cnet.com/health/fda-approves-pfizer-booster-shots-for-those-over-65-and-at-risk-adults/ (CNET)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]]ian [[Ministry of Health (Brazil)|Health minister]] [[Marcelo Queiroga]] tests positive for COVID-19 while in [[New York City]] to attend the [[United Nations General Assembly]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/brazil-health-minister-marcelo-queiroga-covid-19-united-nations/ (CBS News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***Mental health organizations urge the [[Government of Fiji|government]] to address [[suicide prevention]] and the [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on mental health|impact of the COVID-19 crisis on mental health]], as an advisor to the government warns that [[Fiji]] faces a "mental health epidemic". [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/452028/call-for-some-tlc-to-address-mental-health-crisis-in-fiji (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda]]
***[[Uganda]]n [[President of Uganda|President]] [[Yoweri Museveni]] eases COVID-19-related restrictions, including allowing churches and many sports and social activities to resume, due to a decline in the number of infections. The President will also allow universities and other post-secondary education institutions to reopen on November 1. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/uganda-loosens-anti-coronavirus-restrictions-as-pandemic-ebbs/46970642 (Swiss Info)]
*Eight hatchlings from one of the world's rarest crocodile species are found in the [[Sre Pok Wildlife Sanctuary]] in eastern [[Cambodia]], raising hopes for the continuing survival of the species in the wild. Conservationists found the baby [[Siamese crocodile]]s in a river earlier this month, according to a statement from Cambodia's Environment Ministry and the [[World Wildlife Fund]]. [https://www.9news.com.au/world/hatchlings-of-endangered-crocodile-species-found-in-cambodia/f23d0179-db7e-4421-b9d8-bd8a25fb363e (9 News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict]], [[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[King of Saudi Arabia|King]] [[Salman of Saudi Arabia]] insists on the "importance of keeping the Middle East free of weapons of mass destruction ... and support international efforts aiming at preventing [[Iran]] from having nuclear weapons". Salman also accused [[Yemen]]'s [[Houthis]] of launching attacks against the kingdom despite [[Yemeni peace process|proposed ceasefires by Saudi Arabia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/saudi-king-says-kingdom-worked-with-opec-allies-stabilise-oil-market-2021-09-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[France–United States relations]]
**[[French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] and [[U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] agree to meet in Europe soon to repair the strained relations following the security pact between the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia. France also agrees to send back its [[French Ambassador to the United States|ambassador to the United States]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/22/biden-and-macron-agree-to-meet-next-month-in-push-to-repair-ties (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Algeria–Morocco relations]], [[Western Sahara conflict]]
**[[President of Algeria|Algerian President]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] orders the [[Prohibited airspace|prohibition]] of all [[List of airlines of Morocco|Moroccan-registered aircraft]] in [[Algeria|Algerian airspace]] after the two countries broke off diplomatic ties on August 24. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/algeria-closes-airspace-to-all-moroccan-planes-civilian-and-military/ (AFP via ''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Killamarsh killings]]
**The [[Derbyshire Constabulary]] charges a 31-year-old man with four counts of [[murder in English law|murder]] following a suspected [[mass murder]] in [[Killamarsh]], [[Derbyshire]], [[England]], on Sunday. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-derbyshire-58635995 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[COVID-19 protests in Australia]]
**Protesters return to the [[Melbourne city centre|Melbourne CBD]] for the third day straight, albeit in lesser numbers than yesterday. The protests end with a three hour stand-off with [[riot police]] firing non-lethal rounds and teargas at the [[Shrine of Remembrance]]. [[Prime Minister of Australia|Prime Minister]] [[Scott Morrison]] condemns the protests. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/sep/22/melbourne-police-break-up-anti-lockdown-protest-with-non-lethal-rounds-and-teargas (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2021 Tunisian political crisis]]
**[[President of Tunisia|President]] [[Kais Saied]] declares that he will [[rule by decree]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/tunisia-s-saied-issues-decree-strengthening-presidential-powers (AFP via Radio France Internationale)]
*[[2022 Philippine presidential election]]
**[[Mayor of Manila|Mayor]] of [[Manila]] [[Isko Moreno]] announces his candidacy for the [[President of the Philippines]] in the upcoming 2022 elections. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/elections/updates-isko-moreno-launches-candidacy-president-2022 (Rappler)]
*[[Germany]] nominates current [[World Health Organization]] chief [[Tedros Adhanom]] for a second five-year term as the head of the United Nations body. He appears to be the sole candidate, but at a news conference he declines to state whether or not he will accept the nomination. [[government of Ethiopia|Ethiopia]] has withdrawn its support for his candidacy, accusing him of openly supporting the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] in the ongoing [[Tigray War]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210922-tedros-seen-uncontested-for-who-top-job-after-berlin-nod (France 24)]
